study_identification_part.si_3_author_journal_year: Liu et al., Progress in Neuropsychopharmacology & Biological Psychiatry, 2024
study_identification_part.si_4_title: Individualized functional connectome abnormalities obtained using two normative model unveil neurophysiological subtypes of obsessive compulsive disorder

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: Gaussian process regression (GPR) was used to train normative models for functional connectivity strength (FCS) values as a function of age and sex within healthy controls. The model performance was evaluated using 10-fold cross-validation, with standardized mean squared error (MSE) between true and predicted FCS values computed to assess accuracy.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: Subsequently, for each brain region, a Gaussian process regression model was trained to estimate the normative range of FCS values as a function of age and sex within HCs.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.location: Liu2024.pdf.md: Section 2.5 Individualized functional connectivity strength abnormalities

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: Functional Connectivity Strength (FCS) was calculated as the aggregate of connectivity between a given brain region and all other regions. The network nodes were delineated based on a predefined functional parcellation (Brainnetome atlas with 246 regions). Pearson's correlation coefficients were computed between time series of node pairs, followed by Fisher's r-to-z transformation. Only correlations exceeding r=0.2 were included. Whole-brain FCS values were z-score normalized.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: Subsequently, the Functional Connectivity Strength (FCS) values for each brain region were calculated as the aggregate of connectivity between the given region and all other regions. It's noteworthy that our analysis was constrained to correlations surpassing a threshold of r = 0.2, aiming to exclude weak correlations potentially stemming from noise.
nm2_2_response_variable.location: Liu2024.pdf.md: Section 2.4 Functional connectivity strength analysis

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: Age and sex were used as explanatory variables (predictors) in the Gaussian process regression normative model to estimate the normative range of FCS values.
